# `vague-type-name`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: strict · Default: off · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports a public type named by a bare generic word (`Data`, `State`, `Value`)
that does not describe a domain role.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Names such as generic containers or holders force readers to inspect
implementation details to understand responsibility.

## When it fires

Enable the strict profile for codebases that want domain-specific public and
internal type vocabulary.

It reports `pub` container types named by a bare vague word: `Data`, `State`,
`Value`, `Manager`, `Utils` or `Misc`. A qualified name (`ImageData`,
`CheckpointState`, `ResourceManager`) names a role, often the one a
specification it mirrors uses, and `Context` is the protocol name of
`std.hash_map` and `std.sort` contexts, so neither is reported.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
pub const Data = struct { key: u32 };
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Avoid-Redundancy-in-Names>
